record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.context_brief: Complexity of first-order classes of profinite groups
record.original_question: For a first-order sentence φ in the language of groups, determine the descriptive or algorithmic complexity of the class {G : G |= φ} when G ranges over profinite groups.

evidence.quote: Problem 17. For a f.o. sentence φ, what is the possible complexity of {G : G |= φ}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L = \{\cdot, {}^{-1}, e\}$ be the language of groups. A profinite group is a compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected topological group; equivalently, an inverse limit of finite groups. The space of (isomorphism classes of) profinite groups can be equipped with a standard Borel structure (for instance, by coding a profinite group via its inverse system of finite quotients, viewed as an element of a Polish space of countable structures), so that subclasses closed under isomorphism may be analyzed in terms of their descriptive set-theoretic complexity (Borel, analytic, coanalytic, projective hierarchy levels) and, where appropriate, their algorithmic / arithmetical or analytical complexity.

For a first-order sentence $\varphi$ in $L$, regard $\varphi$ as evaluated in a profinite group $G$ using ordinary (discrete) first-order satisfaction. Define
$$\mathrm{Mod}(\varphi) \;=\; \{\, G : G \text{ is a profinite group and } G \models \varphi \,\}.$$

Determine the possible descriptive set-theoretic and algorithmic complexities of classes of the form $\mathrm{Mod}(\varphi)$, as $\varphi$ ranges over first-order sentences in the language of groups. In particular, characterize which levels of the Borel/projective hierarchy (and, in computability-theoretic terms, which levels of the arithmetical or analytical hierarchy on suitable codes) can be attained by such classes, and identify natural upper bounds valid for all first-order $\varphi$ together with sentences witnessing that those bounds are sharp.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a recent list of open problems in computability theory and descriptive set theory. Related work by Nies, Segal, and Tent on expressivity of first-order logic for profinite groups and recent CUNY thesis work on computability-theoretic aspects of profinite groups address partial aspects (e.g., upper bounds for existential and positive theories, axiomatizability of specific profinite groups), but no general classification of the complexity of $\mathrm{Mod}(\varphi)$ for arbitrary first-order $\varphi$ appears to be established.

status_evidence.title: The remarkable expressivity of first-order logic for profinite groups (Nies)
status_evidence.snippet: Many profinite groups are axiomatized by a single first-order sentence; results of Nies, Segal, Tent on expressivity.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial results on expressivity exist but not a full complexity classification.

status_evidence.title: Computability Theoretic Aspects of Profinite Groups (CUNY thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates complexities of first-order theories of profinite groups, with upper bounds for existential and positive fragments.
status_evidence.claim: Partial complexity bounds known for restricted fragments.
